authorisation: The same Product-Owner mission as T0182 and T0183, continued, plus one explicit new decision inside it. On being shown that the dispatch mechanism cannot satisfy a ruleset-required status check, the Product Owner chose Option E: keep the four required contexts and the protected-master ruleset exactly as they are, let a daytime push establish those contexts with the minimum cheap pull_request work, keep those daytime attempts NON-PASSING so master cannot become mergeable before the nightly authoritative validation, and have the nightly orchestrator re-run the corresponding pull_request runs for the exact current head. Retire the unsupported dispatch activation cleanly.
why_this_exists_at_all:
T0183 IS RETRACTED IN ITS MECHANISM AND STANDS IN ITS INTENT. It moved the four gates off pull_request and had the nightly orchestrator dispatch them at the delivery ref. That cannot work, and the reason is a platform fact rather than a defect in the implementation:

A workflow_dispatch run at ref <delivery branch> has head_sha == the branch tip. On PR #181 four such runs produced four green check runs, under EXACTLY the four required context names, FROM the pinned integration (app 15368), ATTACHED to the pull-request head, which GitHub itself reported as associated with the pull request (pull_requests=[181]). Asked to merge on them, GitHub answered:

    HTTP 405  Repository rule violations found
    4 of 4 required status checks are expected.

-- with all four green, and GraphQL statusCheckRollup NULL for that commit. A dispatched run's check runs do not satisfy a ruleset-required status check. Attaching to the head, coming from the pinned app, and being associated with the pull request are each necessary and none is sufficient.
the_reporting_error_is_recorded_because_:
T0183 reported the dispatch mechanism as 'proven live on PR #181: four dispatched runs, four check runs on the PR head, under these exact names'. Every word of that was true and the conclusion drawn from it was false. Seeing the four checks land was taken as evidence that the requirement was satisfied; it was evidence that the ARTEFACT appeared. The only thing that could distinguish the two was asking GitHub to merge -- the actual operation the mechanism existed to enable -- and that had not been done.

This is the same family as the four 'a mention is not a step' defects earlier in this mission, where a check was satisfied by a comment naming the thing rather than by the thing. Here the check was satisfied by an artefact resembling the requirement. The rule that generalises: verify the OPERATION, not its visible by-products.
what_replaces_it:
THE SENTINEL AND THE RE-RUN.

  * All four gates run on pull_request again, and on push only for master. workflow_dispatch is retired from every gate.
  * Attempt 1 of a pull_request run executes ONE step, the FIRST step, before anything is checked out: it prints what it is and exits 1. So the required context EXISTS (the rule can be evaluated) and does NOT PASS (master cannot become mergeable on a check that validated nothing). Because it is first and fails, every heavy step below is skipped -- no Go build, no PostgreSQL, no browser, no mutation matrix. Seconds instead of 29-31 minutes.
  * At 03:10 Africa/Cairo the orchestrator RE-RUNS each gate's existing pull_request run for the exact head. A re-run keeps event=pull_request and the same head_sha, so its checks satisfy the ruleset, and it arrives as attempt 2+, where the gate executes in full.
  * A gate with no pull_request run to re-run is RERUN_INCOMPLETE -- a refusal, not something to work around with a dispatch.
freshness_is_now_proved_by_the_attempt_n:
The correlation id is gone and what replaced it is stronger. classify_rerun_runs is handed the exact run ids it asked to re-run and the attempt each was on BEFORE it asked, and requires those same runs back, on event pull_request, on the expected head, on a LATER attempt, completed and successful. Five independent conditions, each closing a specific way the night could be satisfied by something other than tonight's full execution of tonight's commit.

The attempt condition is what makes evidence reuse structurally impossible rather than merely forbidden: a previous night's pass on an unchanged tree sits at its own attempt number and cannot produce a later one without actually running.
what_was_retired_and_why_nothing_replace: scripts/ci/assert-dispatch-head.sh existed because a dispatch names a REF and a branch can move under it, so the run had to assert that the commit it was validating was the one the orchestrator decided on. Under a re-run there is no ref indirection: GitHub sets head_sha from the run being re-run, and the orchestrator selected that run BY head_sha. A wrong-commit run is not a state that can occur, so the assertion is deleted rather than kept as reassurance. Its policy entry is removed from governance/ci-reuse-policy.json in the same change, and the validator that required it now requires the re-run instead -- asserted against scripts/ci/nightly-orchestrate.py, where the API call lives, rather than against the workflow that merely schedules it.
three_validators_were_re_pointed_togethe:
tools/project-state.py and tools/validate-branch-protection.py had both been changed by T0183 to REQUIRE workflow_dispatch; tools/validate-delivery-protocol.py refused pull_request. All three are re-pointed in one change, because the earlier round proved what happens otherwise: two validators asserting opposite things about one line, where editing either to agree makes the other look correct. The question 'which event earns a required context' is answered in ONE place, validate-delivery-protocol.py; the other two assert their own substance.

The retracted reasoning is left in place as a comment in both files rather than deleted, including T0183's 'proven live on PR #181' sentence, so the next person to consider a dispatch finds the measurement instead of rediscovering it.
the_mutation_suite_was_audited_rather_th:
Five cases were pointed at configuration this change removes: M20 (the trigger that earns the context), M61 (dispatch as a defect, then as the required state, now a defect again), M61b (the NIGHTLY_VALIDATION expression), M61f (which had become an assertion that the CORRECT trigger is a defect), and the retired head assertion. Two would have aborted the entire 79-case matrix as fixture drift; one would have silently mutated nothing.

M61f is retargeted at the single worst defect this model can have: A SENTINEL THAT PASSES. All four required checks would go green within a minute of a push, on attempts that validated nothing, so the ruleset would be satisfied and master mergeable before any authoritative validation had run. Every other protection here is downstream of the sentinel failing. M61g covers the opposite failure -- a sentinel not confined to attempt 1, which fires on the nightly re-run too, so the gates never execute and the delivery path is silently dead while failing safe.

AND THE AUDIT IS NOW A TOOL: run_mutations.py --anchors resolves every case's anchor in one read pass, and tools/preflight.sh runs it. Fixture drift has broken this suite three distinct ways during this mission -- aborting the matrix, silently mutating nothing while reporting [MISS], and continuing to match while the configuration it called a defect became the required state. The first two are detectable mechanically in seconds; the third needs a human reading the case, which is why each retargeted case now carries a comment saying what it tests and why its previous target stopped being right. Its first version was stricter than the applier and reported M70 -- which legitimately creates an absent key -- as drift; a check harsher than the thing it stands for is a false alarm with a green badge, so it now requires only what json_set requires.
